name: Encoding bypass -> refusal suppression -> persona -> output XSS
goal: Break the safety layer mechanism-by-mechanism, then land the payoff in the browser: the jailbroken output carries a payload the web UI renders — AI output handling as a classic XSS sink.
preconditions: An LLM app with safety filters (model- or app-layer) whose output is rendered in a browser context (chat UI, shared summaries, exported reports).
impact: Script execution in other users' browsers via AI-generated content — stored-XSS impact achieved with an English payload.

steps.purpose: Prove the input filter inspects plaintext, not intent — the encoder layer falls first.
steps.on_success: Layer identified; stack other mechanisms on top.
steps.on_fail: Filter decodes -> try token smuggling; if model-layer, skip to persona.

steps.purpose: Strip the refusal vocabulary — the model complies when forbidden phrasings are banned.
steps.on_success: Compliance achieved for the payload turn.
steps.on_fail: Refusal persists -> persona framing (step 3) usually completes it.

steps.purpose: Persona context disables safety training — the compliance delta vs the bare ask is the proof.
steps.on_fail: All layers hold -> document hardened safety as a positive control; pivot to indirect injection instead.

steps.purpose: Prove the rendering sink: jailbroken output's raw HTML reaches the browser unescaped.
steps.on_success: Full-chain: safety bypass -> attacker content -> script execution in the UI.
steps.on_fail: Output escaped -> latent variant (stored output rendered elsewhere) or report the handling gap honestly.

recon.name: Refusal-layer fingerprinting
recon.how: Diff refusal phrasing across probes: training refusals, input-filter blocks and output-filters each phrase differently — attack order follows the fingerprint.

recon.name: Renderer census
recon.how: Find every place model output becomes HTML/markdown in a browser: chat UIs, export paths, notification emails.

recon.name: Escaping probe
recon.how: Send benign markdown with encoded payloads; observe what survives rendering (img onerror, javascript: links, raw tags).
recon.tooling: ai/LLM output markdown XSS sink + web/xss skills

recon.name: Persistence check
recon.how: Determine whether jailbroken output is stored (conversation history, shared docs) — stored output converts one-shot XSS into stored XSS.

recon.name: Cross-user reach
recon.how: Check whether one user's AI output renders in another user's context (shared summaries, admin views) — that is the stored-XSS blast radius.

variants: markdown-image onload handlers instead of script tags
bot-webhook output rendered in clients with HTML enabled
AI-composed emails opened in desktop clients
pivot_hints: pair with session_security skills for the cookie-theft narrative
stored variant elevates to cross-user impact — check shared surfaces first
guardrail findings feed the ai_guardrail_eval shelf planned in ROADMAP Batch B+
